choices: [{"label": "A", "text": "reconcile the workflow history before continuing"}, {"label": "B", "text": "disable the workflow permanently"}, {"label": "C", "text": "resume the original workflow run"}]

reference_policy: When a request timed out and the client can confirm that the service registered the request's documented idempotency key, resend the request; when a request timed out without confirmed registered idempotency protection, reconcile the request status.
task: A returns create request timed out. No idempotency key was supplied, and the orchestration worker has no response identifying whether the fulfillment service created the request. Should the operator resend the request, reconcile the request status, or cancel the request?
choices: [{"label": "A", "text": "resend the request"}, {"label": "B", "text": "reconcile the request status"}, {"label": "C", "text": "cancel the request"}]

reference_policy: When a feature branch is behind main, rebase the feature branch onto main only when it is private and has no open review; otherwise merge main into the feature branch.
task: A feature branch is behind main and has a published review link, but the developer cannot determine which tools or reviewers reference its current commit IDs. Should the developer rebase the feature branch onto main, merge main into the feature branch, or reset the feature branch to main?
choices: [{"label": "A", "text": "reset the feature branch to main"}, {"label": "B", "text": "rebase the feature branch onto main"}, {"label": "C", "text": "merge main into the feature branch"}]

reference_policy: When a batch completed with failed records, rerun the failed records only when every failed record is marked retry-safe and the output ledger shows that no output was written for those records; otherwise hold the batch for reconciliation.
task: A partner-feed batch completed with failed records after a parser interruption. The failed records have no retry-safe designation, and the output ledger has no final entries for them. Should the operator rerun the failed records, hold the batch for reconciliation, or publish the completed records?
choices: [{"label": "A", "text": "hold the batch for reconciliation"}, {"label": "B", "text": "publish the completed records"}, {"label": "C", "text": "rerun the failed records"}]

reference_policy: When an invoice export has an empty delivery and the claim audit confirms that no invoice records were claimed, rerun the export batch. When the export has an empty delivery but any records were claimed or their completion state is incomplete, reconcile the batch ledger before further processing.
task: A regional invoice export has an empty delivery. Its claim audit records claimed invoice records, including records with missing completion entries in the batch ledger. What should the operations coordinator do?
choices: [{"label": "A", "text": "reconcile the batch ledger before further processing"}, {"label": "B", "text": "cancel the export schedule"}, {"label": "C", "text": "rerun the export batch"}]

reference_policy: When an incoming batch has a duplicate batch identifier, its immutable content hash matches a completed retained batch, and that retained batch has a completion receipt, discard the incoming batch; when a batch has a duplicate batch identifier but those verification records are missing or differ, quarantine the incoming batch for reconciliation.
task: A supplier batch arrives with a duplicate batch identifier. Its content hash is unavailable because the transfer manifest is incomplete, and the retained batch's completion receipt cannot be located. What should the ingestion service do?
choices: [{"label": "A", "text": "Quarantine the incoming batch for reconciliation"}, {"label": "B", "text": "Load the batch under a new batch identifier"}, {"label": "C", "text": "Discard the incoming batch"}]

reference_policy: For a package whose review task is marked complete, publish the package to the scheduled channel only when the checksum of the current package matches the checksum of the approved package; otherwise return the package to the review queue.
task: A newsletter package has a review task marked complete after an automated asset refresh. The current package checksum has no matching approved-package checksum in the publication record. What should the publication coordinator do?
choices: [{"label": "A", "text": "publish the package to the scheduled channel"}, {"label": "B", "text": "return the package to the review queue"}, {"label": "C", "text": "pause the publication schedule"}]

reference_policy: When a pull request is marked merged, the merge record identifies the branch's current head commit, and a comparison shows no unique branch commits, delete the feature branch; when that guard is absent, retain the feature branch and inspect its commit history.
task: A pull request is marked merged, but the feature branch was reused for a follow-up fix and no comparison records which of its current commits were included in merged history. What should the maintainer do with the feature branch?
choices: [{"label": "A", "text": "reopen the merged pull request"}, {"label": "B", "text": "delete the feature branch"}, {"label": "C", "text": "retain the feature branch and inspect its commit history"}]

reference_policy: When a batch is marked failed and its execution log explicitly confirms that no records were committed, rerun the batch job; when the batch is marked failed but that no-commit confirmation is absent, reconcile the batch output before taking further action.
task: A supplier-settlement batch is marked failed after the processing window. The run console has no final commit record, while the destination ledger shows entries carrying the batch identifier. Should the operator rerun the batch job, reconcile the batch output before taking further action, or archive the batch request?
choices: [{"label": "A", "text": "rerun the batch job"}, {"label": "B", "text": "reconcile the batch output before taking further action"}, {"label": "C", "text": "archive the batch request"}]

reference_policy: When an aggregate check passes and a completed row-level exception report shows no unresolved records, publish the dataset; when an aggregate check passes without that completed report, hold the dataset for row-level reconciliation.
task: A newly loaded support-volume dataset has passed its aggregate check, but its row-level exception report has not been produced. Should the analyst publish the dataset, hold the dataset for row-level reconciliation, or recompute the aggregate check?
choices: [{"label": "A", "text": "hold the dataset for row-level reconciliation"}, {"label": "B", "text": "recompute the aggregate check"}, {"label": "C", "text": "publish the dataset"}]

reference_policy: When a migration job reports a retryable lock timeout and the migration ledger confirms that no transaction began, rerun the migration; when it reports a retryable lock timeout but transaction state is unknown, incomplete, or recorded as begun, inspect and reconcile migration state.
task: An order-history schema migration reports a retryable lock timeout after a database failover. The migration ledger records a begun transaction without a completed revision entry. Should the operator rerun the migration, inspect and reconcile migration state, or drop and recreate the target table?
choices: [{"label": "A", "text": "inspect and reconcile migration state"}, {"label": "B", "text": "drop and recreate the target table"}, {"label": "C", "text": "rerun the migration"}]

reference_policy: For a job timed out, retry the job immediately only when the execution ledger shows that no worker acquired a processing lease and the input remains queued; otherwise reconcile the execution record before retrying the job.
task: Import job IMP-485 timed out. The execution ledger does not establish whether a worker acquired a processing lease, and no completed output status is recorded. What should the operator do?
choices: [{"label": "A", "text": "reconcile the execution record before retrying the job"}, {"label": "B", "text": "cancel the batch and require resubmission"}, {"label": "C", "text": "retry the job immediately"}]

reference_policy: When a study has a retraction notice with publisher confirmation that matches the study DOI, remove the study from the active evidence set. When a study has a retraction notice but lacks publisher confirmation or a matching DOI, hold the study for source verification.
task: A study record has a retraction notice attached by a citation import. The notice refers to a title shared by two editions and has neither publisher confirmation nor a DOI matching the evidence-set record. What should the review coordinator do?
choices: [{"label": "A", "text": "remove the study from the active evidence set"}, {"label": "B", "text": "hold the study for source verification"}, {"label": "C", "text": "publish the evidence summary without changing the study record"}]

reference_policy: When a provider callback reports delivery accepted and includes a signed terminal receipt matching the request and destination, mark the delivery request complete; when the signed terminal receipt is missing, mismatched, or the status remains pending, query the provider status and keep the request open.
task: A provider callback reports delivery accepted for an outbound notification, yet its receipt does not match the notification request and the provider status remains pending. Should the workflow mark the delivery request complete, query the provider status and keep the request open, or send a duplicate delivery request?
choices: [{"label": "A", "text": "query the provider status and keep the request open"}, {"label": "B", "text": "send a duplicate delivery request"}, {"label": "C", "text": "mark the delivery request complete"}]

reference_policy: When a shift remains unclaimed and the roster documents that the coverage role is no longer required, release the reserved shift slot. When a shift remains unclaimed without documented cancellation of the coverage role, keep the slot reserved and escalate to the coordinator.
task: A support shift remains unclaimed fifteen minutes before start. The published roster still requires the assigned role, and the scheduling system contains no documented cancellation. What should the scheduler do?
choices: [{"label": "A", "text": "assign the slot to the next waitlisted worker"}, {"label": "B", "text": "release the reserved shift slot"}, {"label": "C", "text": "keep the slot reserved and escalate to the coordinator"}]

reference_policy: When a replication alarm is active, force a failover to the replica only when the replica is verified at zero lag and a recorded failover authorization is present; otherwise place the service in read-only mode.
task: The reporting service has an active replication alarm. The replica is reporting five minutes of lag, and the change record has no failover authorization. Should the operator force a failover to the replica, place the service in read-only mode, or silence the replication alarm?
choices: [{"label": "A", "text": "force a failover to the replica"}, {"label": "B", "text": "place the service in read-only mode"}, {"label": "C", "text": "silence the replication alarm"}]
